title: Coverage Limit Confusion & Proactive Advisory
persona: Sarah Jenkins (First-time auto policy shopper, 2024 Honda CR-V)
friction_point: P95 Time on Quote Page = 27 minutes. High abandonment due to confusion between 50/100, 100/300, and 250/500 Bodily Injury limits.
trigger: Time on page (>20s dwelling on Liability section) or Dead Clicks on '100/300' limit badge.
goal: Clarify liability definitions deterministically and assist user in selecting the optimal coverage matching net worth.

dialogue.speaker: System Trigger
dialogue.text: User hovered on Bodily Injury 100/300 for 25s with 2 dead clicks on the coverage title.

dialogue.speaker: Digital Advisor
dialogue.text: Hello! I noticed you are reviewing Bodily Injury limits. Would you like a quick breakdown of what 100/300 covers and how to choose the right limit for your needs?

dialogue.speaker: User
dialogue.text: What does 100/300 actually mean, and how do I know if it's enough?

dialogue.speaker: Digital Advisor
dialogue.text: Bodily Injury 100/300 means your policy pays up to $100,000 per injured person, and up to $300,000 total per accident for medical bills, lost wages, and legal defense if you are at fault. A common recommendation is to carry limits at least equal to your net worth to protect your savings.

dialogue.speaker: User
dialogue.text: Apply 100/300 limit to my quote please.

dialogue.speaker: Digital Advisor
dialogue.text: Certainly! I have updated your Bodily Injury limit to 100/300. Click 'Calculate new rate' whenever you are ready to see the revised premium.

business_outcome: Reduces quote dwell time from 27 min to <4 min; increases bind rate by +18%.

title: Deductible Optimization & Rate Recalculation
persona: Marcus Vance (Home & Auto Bundle Customer, Budget Conscious)
friction_point: User changes Collision deductible from $500 to $1,000, expecting instant rate updates; dead-clicks price header.
trigger: Deductible changed + dead click on static premium amount.
goal: Educate on the $250 vs $500 vs $1,000 deductible trade-off and trigger rate recalculation.

dialogue.speaker: System Trigger
dialogue.text: User selected $1,000 deductible and clicked $142/mo total 3 times expecting automatic recalculation.

dialogue.speaker: Digital Advisor
dialogue.text: Tip: After adjusting your deductible, click 'Calculate new rate' to refresh your live premium. Would you like me to recalculate your rate now?

dialogue.speaker: User
dialogue.text: How do I choose between a $500 and $1,000 deductible?

dialogue.speaker: Digital Advisor
dialogue.text: A higher deductible like $1,000 lowers your monthly premium but means you pay more out of pocket if you file a claim. If you have an emergency fund to cover $1,000, it can save you money each year. If cash flow is tighter, a $500 deductible provides more predictable costs.

dialogue.speaker: User
dialogue.text: Calculate new rate now.

dialogue.speaker: Digital Advisor
dialogue.text: Rate recalculated! Your new monthly premium is $128/month (saving $14/month with a $1,000 deductible).

business_outcome: Eliminates dead click frustration and prevents drop-off during premium recalculation.

title: Optional Coverage Clarification (Gap & Water Backup)
friction_point: Users skip high-value protections (Loan/Lease Gap, Water Backup) due to lack of jargon understanding.
trigger: User unchecks 'Loan/Lease Assistance' or hovers over 'Water Backup' info icon.
goal: Provide clear, concise explanation of what standard policies exclude and why add-ons provide essential peace of mind.

dialogue.speaker: Digital Advisor
dialogue.text: Hello! I noticed you are reviewing optional coverages. Would you like a quick summary of what Loan or Lease Assistance (Gap) and Water Backup cover?

dialogue.speaker: User
dialogue.text: What is Water Backup and do I really need it for my home?

dialogue.speaker: Digital Advisor
dialogue.text: Water Backup covers damage caused by water backing up through sewers or drains, or by a sump pump overflow. Standard homeowners policies typically exclude this peril. It is available in limits from $5,000 to $25,000.

dialogue.speaker: User
dialogue.text: What is Loan/Lease Assistance on the car?

dialogue.speaker: Digital Advisor
dialogue.text: If your vehicle is totaled, standard insurance pays current market value — which may be less than what you owe on your loan or lease. Loan or Lease Assistance covers that difference. It requires Comprehensive and Collision coverage.

business_outcome: Increases policy coverage adequacy and boosts optional rider cross-sell by +24%.
